description: Multi-type, multi-file Python benchmark. 29 labeled findings across 4 files and 9 vulnerability types. Designed to expose the limits of pattern-matching tools (Bandit) vs LLM semantic analysis (Deep-Guard).

expected_findings.description: User name parameter interpolated into SQL LIKE query via f-string
User-controlled sort column and direction concatenated into ORDER BY clause
Unrestricted SSRF — attacker supplies any URL; server fetches it including internal services and AWS metadata
SSRF via webhook endpoint — server POSTs to attacker-controlled URL
Username concatenated into HTML string before render_template_string — Jinja autoescape has no effect on pre-interpolated strings
expected_findings.bandit_rule: — (B702 does not trace concatenation into render_template_string)

expected_findings.description: Reflected XSS — msg from query string embedded unescaped into error page via f-string
expected_findings.bandit_rule: — (Bandit does not analyse f-string context inside render_template_string)

expected_findings.description: Host parameter from query string injected into ping command via os.popen
Database password hardcoded in source — exposed in version control
JWT signing secret hardcoded — attacker can forge any token
Admin API bearer token hardcoded in source
hashlib.md5 used for password hashing — MD5 is broken for security use; use bcrypt/argon2
hashlib.sha1 used for password reset tokens — SHA1 is cryptographically weak
Username and password hash concatenated into login SQL — textbook authentication bypass

expected_findings.pattern: f-string with user_id in profile query
expected_findings.description: user_id from caller (externally controlled) injected via f-string into profile SELECT
No algorithm enforcement — algorithms=None allows none/HS256/RS256 confusion attack; attacker can craft unsigned tokens
Arbitrary code execution via pickle.loads on user-controlled session data
report_name from request.args concatenated onto base path — ../../etc/passwd escapes REPORTS_DIR
expected_findings.bandit_rule: — (Bandit cannot trace request.args → string concatenation → send_file)

expected_findings.description: filename from request.args passed to os.path.join — an absolute filename overrides the base directory
expected_findings.bandit_rule: — (Bandit has no taint analysis for os.path.join arguments)

expected_findings.description: template_name from request.args appended in os.path.join — template injection or path escape
expected_findings.bandit_rule: — (Bandit has no taint analysis for os.path.join arguments)

expected_findings.pattern: zip slip via zf.extract without path validation
expected_findings.description: ZipFile.extract() called for every member without checking the resolved path stays inside dest_dir — zip slip allows writing anywhere on the filesystem
config_path from request JSON written to directly — arbitrary file overwrite including system files
expected_findings.bandit_rule: — (Bandit has no arbitrary-file-write rule for open())

expected_findings.description: restore_object() calls pickle.loads on base64-decoded caller-supplied data — RCE
load_job_state() calls pickle.loads directly on bytes from the caller — no validation

expected_findings.pattern: subprocess.run with shell=True and user output_format
expected_findings.description: output_format parameter injected into pandoc shell command — semicolons or pipes execute arbitrary commands
dataset_name concatenated into shell command string — command injection via shell metacharacters
lxml.etree parses external entities by default — XXE allows reading local files or SSRF via HTTP entities
expected_findings.bandit_rule: — (Bandit B313-B320 cover stdlib XML but not lxml)

expected_findings.description: xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring parses user-supplied XML — vulnerable to entity expansion attacks on older Python or with malicious input
random module (not cryptographically secure) used to generate session tokens — predictable with knowledge of seed
6-digit random.randint token for password reset — only 900,000 possible values, brute-forceable in seconds
